=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/validate_process.sh:125-128 | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The `python3()` wrapper selects `-I` only when the FIRST argument is `-`, `-c`, or `-m`. Any other leading flag (e.g. `-W`, `-X`, `-V`, `--option`) leaves the wrapper defaulting to `-E`. `-E` strips `PYTHON*` environment variables but does NOT disable user-site packages, so a writable `~/.local/lib/pythonX.Y/site-packages` (writable on every GitHub Actions runner) can still inject a checkout-controlled `json.py`/`pathlib.py` into any `python3` call that goes through the wrapper without a leading `-`/`-c`/`-m`. The wrapper is in scripts/validate_process.sh which IS in `LAST_RUN CHANGED FILES`; the case statement is the same code that the PR description and `changelog.d/4506-validation-trust-boundaries.md` claim isolates host-side Python imports.
  WHY: A branch-authored Python invocation like `python3 -W error -c "import json; ..."` would run with `python3 -E -W error -c "..."`. With `-E` only, `sys.path` still contains the user-site directory; a checkout-supplied file placed there is imported before stdlib, defeating the import isolation the changelog advertises. The same defect defeats any future caller of the wrapper with a non-`-`/`-c`/`-m` first arg.
- scripts/validate_process.sh:127 | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: This is the declared-vs-effective capability gap the new code creates. `agents.md:1195-1196` and `changelog.d/4506-validation-trust-boundaries.md:1-2` both declare "host-side Python imports ignore checkout modules" as a security boundary the wrapper enforces, but the case statement only matches three specific first-argument shapes. Any invocation pattern outside those three silently downgrades to `-E`, allowing user-site import hijack despite the documented boundary.
  WHY: Same code path as the SECURITY finding above; included here to surface the gap between declared behavior in operator documentation and effective behavior of the wrapper that establishes the trust boundary.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
